pn_walker.text: I walked from Haworth this morning to see Top Withens. It is a ruin and I loved every damp minute.
The Brontës walked these moors for miles. Their father kept them out in all weathers, which explains the novels.

pn_guide.text: Welcome to Pendle! There is a witch trail every year on the anniversary and a pub that sells a lot of broomsticks.
The real story is sadder than the fun. People who were poor, old and a bit too noisy got accused. I try to tell it straight.

pn_ranger.text: The Quakers still come up here. They sit on the summit in silence. Very peaceful, apart from the wind, which is not a Quaker.

pn_miller.text: My great-gran was a weaver here. Four looms at once, the noise so loud they all learned to lip-read. Half this valley can read lips to this day.
